**Probably yes, but it is not yet confirmed under the run's own rule.**

- Hansen data show 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025, about 3.9% of the 345.6 ha asset.
- JRC maps 98% of that area as forest in 2020, which meets the ≥50% agreement requirement.
- The MGAP 2021 forest map classes 13.1 ha of it as native forest. None is planted forest, and 0.4 ha is outside mapped forest.

The corroboration rule also requires a later year of data showing the loss persisted. 2025 is the latest year available, so that check could not be done. The event is therefore unconfirmed.

The loss data also cannot show the cause. Fire, storm damage or temporary clearing would look the same as permanent deforestation. Treat this as a likely native-forest clearing event that needs confirmation once 2026 data are available, or by checking recent imagery.
